sampling_model.design: Independent sampling of complete recorded trajectories from a finite-horizon behavior process whose action kernel is known and uses only recorded history.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent recorded trajectories, each contributing one multinomial cell in \(\mathcal O\).
sampling_model.treatment: For every complete history \(h\), the conditional behavior action law is \(\mu_t(\cdot\mid O_t(h))\); thus latent rewards do not influence logging beyond their recorded coarsening. The fixed deployment rule \(\pi\) may use latent rewards and is therefore an oracle policy unless a reward-recovery or sensing mechanism is supplied.
sampling_model.overlap: The known kernel satisfies \(\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\ge\epsilon>0\) for every complete-history/action cell, so each deployment-to-logging ratio is finite.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The observed multinomial law is inverted jointly. Fixed-law value images and face systems are certified by global real-algebraic optimization; the exact multinomial confidence fiber itself is used through its defining likelihood-ratio inequality and need not be encoded as a polynomial set.

body.tldr: Finite-horizon MNAR policy value is the image of a compact full-history fiber only after the known recorded-history logger is imposed conditional on every complete latent history. An exact two-stage rational slice has sharp value image \([229/140,26/15]\), rectangular endpoints \(617/420\) and \(19/10\), and two endpoint gaps of \(1/6\). The same elimination refutes the proposed exceptional algebraic equality locus: rectangular equality and strict containment occupy opposite open policy sign chambers. Simultaneous multinomial confidence-fiber inversion covers the whole true identified set with finite-sample probability at least \(1-\alpha\), possibly conservatively.

project_justification.gap: Static weak-shadow programs do not determine whether latent reward completions that separately extremize different continuation values can be pasted into one dynamic law. Moreover, a known policy based on recorded history must be imposed conditional on complete history before the usual deployment-to-logging likelihood ratio is valid.
project_justification.niche: The exact two-stage slice supplies a cell-complete strict-containment certificate under the sound logging restriction and identifies a structural obstruction to the proposed equality-variety headline: equality is an inequality-defined chamber with nonempty interior, not merely a lower-dimensional collision set.
project_justification.fill: The note reports the exact affine completion, signed minors, continuation slopes, rational sharp and rectangular endpoints, and sign-chamber characterization. It replaces the impossible common-zero equality-locus promise by the proved semialgebraic chamber result and adds an exact finite-sample whole-set coverage theorem.

body.related_work: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong's static weak-shadow program remains the one-stage benchmark. Iyengar's finite-horizon robust Bellman recursion assumes rectangular ambiguity, whereas the exact two-stage table here proves that the inverse observed-data fiber need not permit simultaneous stagewise extrema. The stronger proposed claim that equality is confined to an algebraic collision variety is false: the verified policy slice has an open equality chamber and an open strict chamber. Wang, Xu, Lu, and Song's response-model inverse-weighting workflow and Wei, Qu, and Miao's bridge/completeness workflow can be reanalysed against these bounds only after their action mechanism is aligned with the corrected full-history logging equation; their additional point-identifying restrictions should be reported separately rather than built into the partial-identification target. Chen, Christensen, and Tamer motivate confidence-set inversion, while the finite-sample theorem here proves whole-set coverage directly by inclusion of the true-law summand.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact sign characterization is proved on the displayed fixed-observed-law, fixed-logger policy slice. It does not establish that one sign vector is relatively open in the entire space of all compatible two-stage observed laws. More importantly, the requested global common-zero equality variety cannot exist because the slice already contains a full-dimensional open equality chamber away from rank degeneracy and reward-history blindness. A complete-information deployment policy remains operationally unavailable without reward recovery, and confidence-fiber coverage can be conservative.
body.honest_scope: The corrected model imposes the recorded-history behavior kernel conditional on every complete history; under that restriction the pi-over-mu functional is the deployment-policy value. The exact table proof verifies every observed and complete atom, normalization, full-history behavior equations, positivity, weak-shadow cross-products, affine feasibility box, signed minors, continuation determinants, sharp image, rectangular endpoints, and strict gaps. It also proves a negative result: no finite common-zero polynomial family can characterize all equality points after only the advertised rank and policy exceptions are removed. Accordingly, no field-tier generic equality-variety claim is made. The whole-set confidence region has exact finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for the entire true identified set, with model compatibility needed only for nonvacuity.
body.interpretation: In the verified two-stage design, compute \(M_7=-x_0+3x_1-2x_2\) from the oracle policy's reward-specific second-stage action probabilities. If \(M_7>0\), the first- and second-stage programs select opposite completion faces and both rectangular endpoints are too wide; if \(M_7\le0\), they share extremizers and the rectangular endpoints are exact. This diagnostic is exact for the printed rational slice, not a universal polynomial ideal for all two-stage tables.
